answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs m-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a key additive within the perovskite precursor solution, while p-F-PEACl is entirely absent. Analysis of the CONTROL performance (PCE: 23.606%, Voc: 1.17607 V, Jsc: 25.3513 mA/cm², FF: 79.1751%) reveals significant limitations tied to this choice. The m-MeO-PEACl additive, while intended for surface and grain boundary passivation, exhibits suboptimal defect suppression due to the electron-donating methoxy group. This group reduces the binding strength with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions at perovskite interfaces, leaving residual trap states that promote non-radiative recombination. Consequently, the CONTROL device suffers from voltage losses (evidenced by the Voc deficit relative to the theoretical limit) and a depressed fill factor, indicating substantial recombination and series resistance issues. The methoxy group’s hydrophilic nature may also exacerbate moisture-induced degradation pathways, though performance metrics primarily reflect immediate electrical losses. In contrast, p-F-PEACl—though unused in CONTROL—leverages the strong electron-withdrawing fluorine substituent, which enhances Lewis acid-base interactions with Pb²⁺ defects. This stronger binding passivates deep-level traps more effectively, suppresses ion migration, and improves interfacial energy level alignment, directly targeting the Voc and FF limitations observed. Crucially, maintaining the same 2.0 mg/mL concentration avoids trade-offs like insulating layer formation or disrupted crystallization, as the fluorine moiety’s compact size preserves film morphology without introducing steric hindrance. Other formulation elements (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L, MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, 4,4,4-NA SAM at 0.5 mg/mL, PDADI passivator at 0.5 mg/mL) remain optimal as-is, as their roles in bulk crystallization, interface stabilization, and secondary passivation are uncompromised in CONTROL and require no adjustment.  

The proposed formulation change specifically addresses the interfacial recombination bottleneck by substituting m-MeO-PEACl with p-F-PEACl. This modification elevates Voc by minimizing surface recombination velocity, directly increasing the quasi-Fermi level splitting. Simultaneously, reduced trap-assisted recombination at grain boundaries lowers series resistance, boosting FF through improved charge extraction. Jsc sees marginal gains from suppressed ion migration, which stabilizes the bandgap and minimizes current hysteresis. The resulting performance improvements manifest as a Voc range of 1.166–1.206 V, Jsc range of 25.39–25.79 mA/cm², FF range of 83.9–85.9%, and PCE range of 24.8–26.7%. These gains stem from the fluorine group’s superior electrostatic passivation, which mitigates the voltage-dependent carrier loss mechanisms inherent to the CONTROL device without altering processing dynamics.  

Implement the following composition adjustments:  
- Replace m-MeO-PEACl with p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution.  
- Retain all other formulation variables unchanged: Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L, MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, 4,4,4-NA SAM at 0.5 mg/mL, and PDADI passivator at 0.5 mg/mL.

A SAM solution, consisting of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL), was added to facilitate a stable perovskite interface. The addition of MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and m-MeO-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) as additives were carefully prepared. The perovskite precursor solution was then spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s followed by an additional spin at 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 15 s of the spinning, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. Next, the substrates were quickly transferred for annealing at 110 ℃ for 15 min. The passivator PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was introduced into the system to improve material properties. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
